patch.value: Divergence means the magnitude grows; oscillation means the sign alternates. D alternates but shrinks, so it converges slowly; B alternates and grows. For a quadratic loss under full-batch gradient descent the loss itself decreases monotonically whenever the run converges, so look at the parameters (or a multi-dimensional, noisy or non-quadratic loss) to see oscillation.

Divergence means the magnitude grows; oscillation means the sign alternates. D alternates but shrinks, so it converges slowly; B alternates and grows. Here the parameter trajectory reveals oscillation. For a convex quadratic loss under full-batch gradient descent, the loss itself decreases monotonically whenever the run converges, in one dimension or many, so oscillation shows up in the parameters; it appears in the loss curve mainly for noisy (mini-batch) or non-quadratic problems.
